subject: math
title: Adding and Subtracting to 1000
seo_title: Grade 3 Adding and Subtracting to 1000 Worksheets: Regrouping and Mental Math (Ontario)
standard_text: Represent and solve problems involving the addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 1000, using various tools and algorithms
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on adding and subtracting to 1000, matched to the Ontario curriculum: mental math, column addition and subtraction with regrouping, subtracting across zeros, checking with the inverse and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key. Great EQAO practice.
key_big: Line up hundreds, tens and ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: Adding: if a column makes 10 or more, regroup 1 into the next column. Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column. Check with the inverse: add back what you took away.
body_html:
The idea: hundreds, tens and ones

Every number is made of hundreds, tens and ones. Split the numbers. Add the hundreds, the tens and the ones. Then put the parts back together.

If the ones make 10 or more, regroup: 10 ones make 1 ten.

Mental math: jump and compensate

On an open number line, start at the first number. Jump the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compensate

What is 375 + 198?

198 is 2 less than 200. 375 + 200 = 575. You added 2 too many, so take 2 away: 575 − 2 = 573.

Answer: 573

Column addition: regroup when a column makes 10 or more

Put ones under ones, tens under tens and hundreds under hundreds. Start with the ones on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

Column subtraction: regroup when the top digit is smaller

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column as 10.

Across zeros: if there are 0 tens, regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens first. Then regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. The 0 tens become 9 tens.

Check with the inverse

Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check a subtraction, add the answer and the number you took away. To check an addition, subtract one number from the total.

Check

Is 500 − 168 = 332 right?

Add back what you took away: 332 + 168 = 500. You get the starting number, so it is right.

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not regrouping (367 + 258 = 515)Write the regrouped 1 in the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (452 − 178 = 326)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Lining up the columns wrongly (346 + 52 = 866)Line up the ones on the right: 346 + 52 = 398
Making the 0 tens into 10 tens (500 − 168 = 342)One ten moves to the ones, so 10 tens become 9 tens

faq.q: What does Grade 3 learn about adding and subtracting in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Students add and subtract whole numbers that add up to no more than 1000. They use mental math, tools like base ten blocks and number lines, and algorithms such as the column method to solve problems.

faq.q: What is regrouping in Grade 3 math?
faq.a: Regrouping means trading 10 of one place for 1 of the next, such as 10 ones for 1 ten. Older books call it carrying or borrowing.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 500 − 168?
faq.a: Regroup 1 hundred as 10 tens, then 1 ten as 10 ones. 500 becomes 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, so 500 − 168 = 332.

faq.q: Is adding and subtracting on the Grade 3 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, and adding and subtracting whole numbers is part of the Grade 3 Number strand. Many questions are word problems.

items.q: Which addition checks 523 − 168 = 355?
items.e: To check a subtraction, add the answer and the number you took away. You should get the number you started with: 355 + 168 = 523.

items.q: Which subtraction checks 384 + 279 = 663?
items.e: To check an addition, start with the total and take away one of the numbers. You should get the other number: 663 − 279 = 384.

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 245 + 318 = 563?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers: 245, 318 and 563. The total minus one part gives the other part: 563 − 245 = 318. (563 − 318 is 245, not 254.)
